newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli Arabs head for Syria to uphold peace hopes.
newsitem.headline: Israeli Arabs head for Syria to uphold peace hopes.

text.p: An Israeli Arab delegation, including members of Israel's parliament, headed for Syria on Thursday to tell President Hafez al-Assad not to abandon hopes for peace.

The 50 delegates, including Druze and politicians from the opposition Labour and Meretz parties, will meet Syrian officials and Palestinian groups during an eight-day stay, Palestinian sources in Damascus said.
Saleh Tarif, a Druze delegate who is also an Israeli reserve captain, told army radio at the airport before their departure that he and the others would meet Assad.
"It's the first time a reserve army officer (from Israel) will shake the hand of the Syrian president," he said.

Labour and Meretz, dovish partners in the last government, favour swapping Golan Heights land for peace with Syria -- a policy opposed by right-wing Likud Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who was elected last year.

Last month Netanyahu joined in giving preliminary approval to a bill that would make it harder for parliament to cede the Golan Heights. Israel has held the territory for 30 years and Syria demands its return.

"Opposite the prattle and slogans of the Netanyahu government and the decision reinforcing the Golan Law, we must present ourselves in full force in order to tell the Syrians there are those who support peace and not to abandon hope," Tarif said.
Arabs make up about 17 percent of Israel's population.
